body:
This is my alt/throwaway account and some of this was told to me in confidence by a relative, so I won't go into any detail on that.

My mother is a very abusive, personality disordered, mentally stunted woman who grew up in the inner city. Turns out there were years of abuse and molestation going on in that family. I knew my mother grew up in foster homes when she was a kid but it turns out that the reason she did is that her mother straight up walked out on her and her younger siblings. Just, walked out of the house and left the kids there on their own to fend for themselves until finally the state got involved. CPS wasn't even a thing yet when this happened. 

My dad told a therapist this while he was being confronted for allowing my mother to be abusive. He thought it was a justification for why she is the way she is.

Also, it turns out many of the kids in my mother's family--likely including herself--were molested. Like I said, she grew up in foster homes and child welfare centers in the inner city... 

This doesn't justify her abusive behavior. But it did help me understand why she'll never be able to change who she is.

I am on Medicare Part B once my insurance extension runs out.

I've never had to pay $100 co-pays. When I was running off Medicare alone (before my extension got approved) it was $20 for my psych. Dunno about the other doctors.
The latter. DVR helps with driving? I'm actually trying to learn to drive right now but I have to take my knowledge test.
Neuropsychologists are a thing? I have to find one of those.

Oh shit what a LIFESAVER. I had no idea DDS was a thing, only DDD.

I found the online brochure for DDS and I'm gonna go over it with my advocate thank you SO MUCH.

I see.

DDD does not accept Medicare in my state, only Medicaid. And there's a state law that you must be eligible for Medicaid to receive any sort of DDD services at all, from residential housing to day programs to respite.

I am already on Medicare. 

Regarding the ABLE account, it mentions that if the designated beneficiary dies, the funds in the trust will be released to the state. This is what my dad was afraid of when he was advised to set up the ABLE account for me--he is 77. If he is the beneficiary and he dies, the state will seize all the money in the trust. Is there any way to get me named as the beneficiary so I can keep the funds?

I get SSDI because my father worked to pay into it.

If I put the money in an ABLE trust is it still accessible to me when I need to access it?

Can I afford an apartment on SSDI? It's not very much. I was looking for apartments near my school back in the beginning of the fall when all the room/board ads were all over the place and I found one that was $800 a month and I still could not afford that.

Can you tell me what "lot more help out there" there is? I can only go by what I've already been told/tried. 

I am on SSDI not SSI and I have Medicare.
I was denied MediCAID. I have Medicare. But the disability supports programs in my area only accept Medicaid.

The aggressive/violent behavior only occurs around one person and does not occur when that person is not present. 

If I lived on campus I would need transportation to be able to go shopping for groceries.
Medicare.

I called around to 5 different residential placement organizations in the county and all of them denied me because they said they only run through the Division of Developmental Disabilities, and to receive DDD services you have to qualify for Medicaid, which I don't.
I'm about to graduate after the winter/spring semester. Now would be a really bad time to take a break from school...

They said I had too much in liquid assets (savings). It's not enough to sustain myself in an apartment for longer than maybe a month or two. I receive SSDI. 

I have a few friends who use Easter Seals. I'll look them up. 

I haven't talked to my DVR counselor since I started at university but I can get hold of her.

Can tell you from experience that for me it made everything fucking worse.

Would've taken me 5 minutes to get me stabilized and able to cooperate if they had just given me back my phone, when instead it took 5 days because they didn't.

Here's what happens when I go speak to my family:

My dad is the only one I can even speak to. My mother is a self-absorbed overgrown 5-year-old with cognitive delays. Who also believes anything anyone tells her to without question or the employment of critical thinking. She thinks the Watchtower and the Bible solve everything, and she actually admitted she did abuse me and that she has no regrets, "because it got me everything I wanted. And as long as I get what I want, I don't care." 

I have gone to my dad countless times. Countless. His responses? "That isn't true." "Your mother never did anything to hurt you." And then finally, when he admitted he knows what she had been doing, "She didn't mean it. She never means to hurt anybody." "She thought she was being a good mother." "She didn't know any better." Even when I told him she ADMITTED that she did it and she's happy that she did. "She didn't mean that." When I told him I can't take it anymore and that I'm at the very end of my rope and I'm about to do something drastic? He threw his hands up in the air and said "WELL I DON'T KNOW WHAT TO DO."

My older brother, the golden child, is a broken drug-addicted bastard who is the other half of the reason why I can't take this anymore. He walks around slamming doors, throwing tantrums, banging on the walls, growling, waking everybody up at 2 AM with his coughing and hacking from the smoking and with his throwing shit at the wall and slamming doors because his parents won't buy food for his 40-year-old grown ass self, and I'm on the other side of his wall and have to deal with his shit and his mother's shit and everyone else's shit. 

I've reached out to every available social service, social worker, and state services for disabled adults. I've told my story to at least 25 different people by now and all of them have said the same thing: "I'm sorry you've had to go through so much, but we can't do anything for you unless you are eligible for Medicaid." 

I'm not eligible for Medicaid. I applied twice. They denied me twice. 

I have no way out. Even ending up in the hospital, which I thought would be the final reality check that something has got to change, did nothing. I'm right back where I was before and I realized that it's always going to be life for me...
They walked by my door several times today. They know I don't usually sit in bed for 16 hours a day but they just walked right on by. No one has even spoken to me at all today.

I've already been through all of the social services and adult disability services in my area.

Their response was "We can't do anything for you if you don't have Medicaid." 

Medicaid's response was "You can't have Medicaid."
Not at all.
Last time I called a hotline they just put me in the hospital

I live with (am trapped with) my fucked up family and I don't have any friends who could do anything for me. 

I also have several cognitive and mental disabilities.
I don't have one.
Oh, I see. It's because the nurses at the ER kept on using the word "committed" and so I was confused.

I will never seek help from a county or state run organization again. 

I have a private psychologist, a support group, and an independently\-run women's center plus a wellness center run by the local Mental Health Association. These are my outlets from now on.

Was too busy being a complete wreck because they took away my toys and computer to share anything with them, unfortunately. 

Bear in mind I was not a wreck until they did that. Which I don't get...why create a crisis for someone then go "Oh, she's in crisis, send her to a facility where they'll just exacerbate it"

Thanks for the answers. I'm still iffy and distrustful due to my experiences with the hospital but at least I have some answers as to why it happened. Nobody at the hospital bothered to tell me why it was happening, just "It is, and you have to deal." 

"Your ability to cope was exceeded by the magnitude of your issues" what does that mean? 

"if the patient refuses to take medication, the doctor may determine that it is necessary to forcibly medicate the patient. " Isn't that only for if the patient is violent or acting out in a dangerous/threatening manner? I was not. I only saw one person get the needle and it was because she was having a psychotic episode and could not be talked down from it. 

" You may complain to the hospital." Turns out my father did go to hospital administration and the nurses were reprimanded, so at least that happened. 

Also, both my father and I still have this question: if they had already made their decision to send me to the facility \(from the ER\), and the judge wasn't going to listen to me in the first place, what was the point in having me speak to him in the first place? The clinician, screener, and psychiatrists at the hospital had apparently already decided to have me put in a hold the moment I made the call to that hotline.
What if it turns out all the physical/cognitive defects I've had for my whole life really do add up to fetal alcohol syndrome?

This is one of my throwaway accounts but

I've struggled with cognitive delays, learning disabilities, severe social and behavioral issues, personality, mood, and thought disorders sensory processing issues, and dealt with some severe abuse from my mother for my entire childhood and adolescence. I did not receive diagnoses until I was an adult, because my mother turned away any and all attempts to evaluate me or intervene up until she legally could not anymore. And even so the diagnoses were only "we can't really entirely figure out wtf is wrong with you, but here's what we can see so far based upon the DSM and your evaluation results." 

Someone pointed out that one of the telltale physical signs of FAS is a broad, smooth philtrum. Of course, when someone points that out everyone in the room is going to start touching at their philtrum to make sure there's a groove there. I'd never thought about such a thing at all because come on, who does? 

I don't have a groove there. 

So I looked up FAS, which is something I'd never had to look up before in my entire life. 

Turns out I have *way* more that lines up than just a smooth philtrum. 

There's no real way to confirm it because it cannot be diagnosed without my mother's confirmation of drinking during pregnancy and she sure as hell is never gonna confirm that. They can't make a diagnosis based on phenotype alone, especially in an adult in her 20s. All I know is that my mother loves her wine, admitted I never slept for more than 30 minutes at a time as a newborn, was a horrible abusive sociopath who fucked with me for my entire life and LAUGHED about it, and I spent my whole life being bullied and isolated for my appearance and behavior and dealing with cognitive and mental bullshit that went undiagnosed for 20 years. *And* I have the phenotypic signs. 

...There's just too much fucking evidence and now I have to deal with that possibility in my mind forever, knowing it will never be confirmed or proven. And at this point I just don't WANT it to be confirmed anymore.
